study type: Mixed-methods study: retrospective cohort study (clinical data analysis) and in-vitro experimental study (cellular experiments)
exposure: Glucose concentration variations (from high to low levels)
outcome: Alterations in HUVEC gene expression (related to metabolism, inflammation, oxidative stress, diabetes signalling pathways)
cohort: The study analyzed clinical data from 68 healthy pregnant women and 67 pregnant women diagnosed with GDM, and utilized human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVECs) obtained from six pairs of pregnant women.
finding: Alterations in glucose concentration, especially the shift from high to low levels, can lead to vascular endothelial cell dysfunction, increased ROS levels, and activation of the TGF-b/SMAD3 signalling pathway, which can influence the microenvironment and potentially compromise maternal and fetal health.
cross-section timing: Data was collected retrospectively from early pregnancy through birth.
